subject.title: [Bug] Webchat avatar endpoint /avatar/{agentId} returns 404 even with valid IDENTITY.md avatar

question: Should unresolved local avatars keep returning a generic 404 from direct `/avatar/{agentId}` while safe reasons are exposed through metadata/UI, or should the raw endpoint expose specific 4xx errors such as 413 for oversized files?
rationale: The current source can avoid broken UI through metadata, but changing the raw image endpoint would change the local file-serving disclosure boundary and public HTTP behavior.

options.title: Keep raw 404, improve UI diagnostics
options.body: Preserve the current file-serving boundary and use safe metadata to suppress broken webchat images and show clear missing/too-large/unsupported feedback.

options.title: Expose selected raw 4xx errors
options.body: Return specific statuses from `/avatar/{agentId}` only after maintainers define which policy reasons are safe to disclose to authenticated browser clients.

options.title: Close after fork cleanup
options.body: If maintainers consider current settings/docs feedback sufficient, close or reject the conflicting fork PR first and then close this issue as implemented enough.

recommendation.title: Keep raw 404, improve UI diagnostics
recommendation.body: Preserve the current file-serving boundary and use safe metadata to suppress broken webchat images and show clear missing/too-large/unsupported feedback.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal for the avatar resolver, route hardening, and local-file security boundary.
